key_insight: A five-qubit AME state enabled parallel teleportation of two qubits on IBM quantum hardware, preserving entanglement on both channels after three rounds.
engineering_relevance: Compact Clifford decoders support reconfigurable two-channel quantum communication, with lower circuit depth and dynamical decoupling helping preserve fidelity.
method: Constructed three-qubit decoders using three logical two-qubit gates for each of 60 inequivalent sender–receiver assignments.
Combined parallel operations, classical Pauli-frame post-processing, and XY4 dynamical decoupling.
evidence_signal: With XY4 and the lowest-cost decoder, final entanglement fidelities were 0.704 ± 0.028 and 0.680 ± 0.022 across eight trials; both pointwise 99% confidence-interval lower bounds exceeded the 0.5 separability threshold.
watch_item: The demonstration is limited to two channels and three teleportation rounds; scalability to larger networks remains unestablished.
paper_title: Parallel Teleportation via AME(5,2) States on IBM Quantum Hardware
